item.title: He Hid His Roommate’s Remains In A Bus Terminal
item.description: After Swiss dance student Monika Beerle was killed in 1989, police found her remains at New York’s Port Authority Bus Terminal. Her roommate, Daniel Rakowitz, was found not guilty by reason of insanity in 1991 and committed to a secure psychiatric hospital

item.title: A Phone Monitoring App Exposed His Teacher’s Abuse
item.description: Arizona teacher Brittany Zamora’s abuse of a 13-year-old student came to light when his parents checked his phone using a monitoring app. She tried to persuade them not to contact police. In 2019, she pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 20 years in prison.

item.title: The Royal Dresser Whose Life Ended In Murder
item.description: Jane Andrews spent nine years working as a dresser for Sarah, Duchess of York, before her life took a dramatic turn. In 2000, she killed her boyfriend, businessman Thomas Cressman, after their relationship collapsed. Andrews was convicted of murder in 2001 and sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: He Killed His Family Before A Planned School Shooting
item.description: Nicholas Prosper murdered his mother and two younger siblings in Luton in 2024. Investigators later uncovered his plan to attack his former primary school, but he was arrested before carrying it out. He pleaded guilty and received life with a minimum term of 49 years.
